passages.title: From a village to the city
passages.text:
Last year I left my small village in Wales and moved to Manchester to start my first job. I had never lived anywhere bigger (1) ______ our local market town, so I was quite nervous.

At first, everything felt strange. I was afraid (2) ______ getting lost, so I carried a map everywhere, and at night the noise of the traffic kept me awake. I didn't know anyone in the city, and neither (3) ______ my flatmate, who had just arrived from Spain. We spent most evenings watching television in our tiny kitchen.

Things got better when I found (4) ______ about a climbing club near my office. We went along together one evening, and now we go twice a week. Most of our friends here are people we met on the climbing wall.

These days I really enjoy city life. (5) ______ is always something to do, from free concerts in the park to street markets at the weekend. Rents are expensive, and I sometimes miss the quiet countryside. At (6) ______ same time, I can't imagine going back now. Moving to Manchester was one of the best decisions of my life.

questions.question: Gap (1): I had never lived anywhere bigger ____ our local market town.
questions.explanation: 'Bigger' is a comparative adjective, so it must be followed by 'than' before the thing it is compared with ('our local market town'). No other word can link a comparative to its second part.

questions.question: Gap (2): I was afraid ____ getting lost, so I carried a map everywhere.
questions.explanation: The adjective 'afraid' is followed by the preposition 'of' + noun or -ing form ('afraid of getting lost'). 'About', 'for' or 'to' do not work before 'getting' here.

questions.question: Gap (3): I didn't know anyone in the city, and neither ____ my flatmate.
questions.explanation: 'Neither + auxiliary + subject' means 'also not'. The first verb is in the past simple negative ('didn't know'), so the auxiliary must be 'did'. 'Was' or 'had' do not match 'didn't know'.

questions.question: Gap (4): Things got better when I found ____ about a climbing club near my office.
questions.explanation: 'Find out (about something)' is a phrasal verb meaning 'discover information'. Without 'out', 'found about' is not correct English.

questions.question: Gap (5): ____ is always something to do, from free concerts in the park to street markets.
questions.explanation: 'There is' introduces something that exists: 'There is always something to do'. 'It is always something to do' is not correct, because 'it' needs something to refer back to.

questions.question: Gap (6): At ____ same time, I can't imagine going back now.
questions.explanation: 'At the same time' is a fixed expression meaning 'but also / however'. 'Same' always takes 'the' in this phrase; 'a same time' or 'this same time' are not used.
